EDEN Support-kit module template  
Write one support-kit module in this document, then export it as Markdown. A short script turns the export into a module page for the kit.

# **How to use this template**

> 1. Make your own copy: File \> Make a copy. Name the copy after your module.  
> 2. Fill in the table under **Module metadata**. Replace every text in \[square brackets\]. Leave a row empty if it does not apply.  
> 3. Write the module under **Module content**. Keep the section headings (Heading 2), change their text if you need to, and add more Heading 2 or Heading 3 sections as needed.  
> 4. In **Recommendations**, write one action per bullet. They become a checklist readers can tick.  
> 5. Share the copy with your WP3 colleagues for comments. When it is ready: File \> Download \> Markdown (.md).  
> 6. Put the .md file in the kit repository and run **python3 var/gdoc\_to\_module.py your-file.md**. The script writes the module page into the right folder and reports anything missing.

Keep headings and lists as real Google Docs headings and bullets (not bold text or typed dashes), so the Markdown export keeps them.

# **Module metadata**

| Field | Value | How to fill it |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Title | \[Module name\] | What the module is about, task first, under 8 words. Example: Preparing deposits |
| Description | \[One sentence\] | One sentence shown on cards and in search results. |
| Role | \[researcher\] | Who it is for: researcher, manager, trainer, or anyone. |
| I want to | \[what the reader wants to do\] | The user story. Start lower case, no full stop. Example: prepare my files for deposit, with sustainable formats and basic checks |
| So that | \[why it matters to them\] | The benefit. It should add something the title does not already say. |
| Short task | \[prepare my files for deposit\] | Under 45 characters. Shown in the home page's "I want to…" menu. |
| Kind of help | \[how-to\] | how-to (get it done), tutorial (learn by doing), reference (look it up) or explanation (understand why). |
| Order in the role path | \[1\] | Position among the modules for this role. A number. |
| Disciplines | \[all\] | Comma-separated, or all. |
| Data types | \[all\] | Comma-separated, or all. |
| Keywords | \[deposit, file formats\] | Comma-separated. Used by search. |
| Processes it mainly teaches | \[CPP-010\] | 1 to 3 WP1 Core Preservation Process IDs, comma-separated. List: eosc-eden.github.io/wp1-cpp-descriptions |
| Other processes it applies | \[CPP-001, CPP-002\] | Other CPP IDs the module touches. Keep it to the ones a reader would act on. |
| Frameworks cited | \[cts-2026: R14; eosc-tf-fm\] | framework: requirement codes, separated by semicolons. Frameworks: cts-2023, cts-2026, nestor, iso-16363, oais, premis, eosc-tf-fm. |
| Related modules | \[reviewing\_deposits\] | File names of related modules, comma-separated. |
| Contributors | \[Your name\] | Names as listed in the kit's contributor list (with ORCID). Comma-separated. |
| Status | draft | draft or ready. |

# **Module content**

\[Opening paragraph: two to four sentences on why this task matters and what the reader will have when they finish. It appears at the top of the module page.\]

## **Considerations**

\[One line introducing the questions, for example: Key aspects to consider include:\]

> * \[A question the reader should ask about their data or process\]  
> * \[Another question\]

## **Recommendations**

> * \[One concrete action, starting with a verb\]  
> * \[Another action\]
